newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ted Turner blasts U.S. veto, rival Murdoch.
newsitem.headline: Ted Turner blasts U.S. veto, rival Murdoch.

text.p: Media mogul Ted Turner blasted the United States government on Friday for vetoing the re-election of U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, attacked business rival Rupert Murdoch and said Britain always does what the United States asks it to do.
And that was just in the first few minutes of a speech to a forum of television executives from five continents at the United Nations on the global impact of television.

With Boutros-Ghali seated nearby, Turner asked, "Who is the United States to stand alone against the re-election of this good man here?" Saying he loved the United Nations, he also called on the United States to pay its $1.4 billion debt to the world body.

Amid applause and shouts of "bravo," Turner said, "I just ask that the United States reverse its position and go along ... We believe in democracy. That means the majority rules and the majority voted 14 to one," he said, referring to a vote in the Security Council on Tuesday to re-elect Boutros-Ghali.
"Even England voted to re-elect this man and England always does what the United States asks them to do."

Turner said he thought about buying the U.S. debt from the United Nations "and giving my IOU to the U.S. government." But "I thought it would be a grandstand play and I would be criticized for doing it. So pay up. You owe the money, you pay it."

He declared himself a strong believer in local control of television and blasted Murdoch, head of Sydney, Australia-based The News Corp Ltd, saying, "We were very benign. Now, already you can see that there is a new group coming, led by that no-good SOB (son of a bitch) Rupert Murdoch. "They want to control the world. They want to control the television world. We have got to do everything we can to stop them."

Again excoriating his Australian-born rival, Turner said: "Rupert Murdoch, sitting wherever he is -- I don't know what country he is supposedly from, he is truly a citizen of the world -- he wants to sit here and control Indian television in India, he wants to control Chinese television in China. Bullshit! I don't know how that translates into other languages."

Turner, who founded Cable News Network (CNN), is now vice-chairman of Time Warner Inc media conglomerate, which has refused to broadcast Murdoch's Fox News Channel, a competitor of CNN in New York, the biggest cable market.

Asked later by a participant in the forum how peace could be made between himself and Murdoch, Turner replied: "That is a battle between good and evil. I don't want to talk about that no-good bastard anymore."

Later, a spokesman for News Corp asked, "Was Ted Turner speaking on behalf of the officers and directors of Time Warner or are those officers and directors prepared to disown Mr. Turner's vulgar remarks?"
